texts: In this infant with a large VSD, echo would show left atrial dilation, left ventricular dilation, a left-to-right shunt and right ventricular hypertrophy: all of the above.
The shunt sends extra blood round the lungs and back to the left atrium and ventricle, which dilate; the right ventricle thickens against the high pulmonary pressure.
The loud holosystolic murmur at the left lower sternal border, the poor feeding, sweating and fast breathing and the big heart on the chest film are the picture of a large shunt in heart failure.
In the picture, the bat sees all four at once: the rush through the hole, the swollen red lobby and engine room and the thick blue walls.
Memory hook: a big hole floods the red side and thickens the blue.
